sections.title: Your mission
sections.body: Learn the fictional Pulse API well enough to plan a reliable integration.

sections.title: Pulse API quickstart
sections.content: Pulse accepts events through POST /v1/events. Each request needs an Authorization bearer token and a unique Idempotency-Key. Successful acceptance returns 202 with an event_id; processing is asynchronous and is not complete at acceptance. Query GET /v1/events/{event_id} until status is processed or failed. The API allows 60 requests per minute and returns 429 with Retry-After when the limit is exceeded. Temporary unavailability returns 503 and may also include Retry-After; that response does not by itself mean the client exceeded a rate limit. A Retry-After value uses either delay seconds or an HTTP-date. Reusing an idempotency key returns the original event rather than creating a duplicate. This quickstart does not define a polling interval, maximum polling duration, idempotency-key retention period or same-key/different-payload behavior; these are open questions to confirm before production rather than defaults to invent.

provenance.adaptationNote: API product names, endpoints, headers, identifiers, rate limits and metrics are fictional training data; only HTTP status-code and Retry-After semantics are referenced from the cited RFCs.

expressions.phrase: The documentation guarantees ___, but it does not define ___.
expressions.meaning: Separate an explicit API contract from an unresolved detail.
expressions.example: The documentation guarantees asynchronous acceptance, but it does not define the polling interval.
alternatives: The documented behavior is ___; ___ remains an open question.

expressions.meaning: Contrast two response classes without merging their causes.
expressions.example: A 429 response indicates rate limiting, whereas 503 indicates temporary unavailability.

expressions.meaning: Turn an undocumented behavior into a concrete follow-up instead of an invented default.
expressions.example: Before production, I would confirm the polling limits and idempotency-key retention period.
alternatives: I would treat ___ as an open question and verify it with the API owner.

exercises.question: Why must the client query event status?
options: A 202 response means the event was processed and the final result is already stored.
A 202 response means the event was accepted but processing is not complete.
correctAnswer: A 202 response means the event was accepted but processing is not complete.
exercises.explanation: Acceptance and final processing are separate states.

exercises.question: Which statement distinguishes 429 from 503 correctly?
options: 429 means the caller exceeded a rate limit; 503 means temporary unavailability and is not proof of rate limiting.
429 means the service is temporarily unavailable; 503 means the caller exceeded a rate limit of 60 requests per minute.
503 means the event was processed successfully and needs no retry.
correctAnswer: 429 means the caller exceeded a rate limit; 503 means temporary unavailability and is not proof of rate limiting.
exercises.explanation: The quickstart assigns different causes to the two statuses even though either response can carry Retry-After.

exercises.question: Which implementation detail remains an open question?
options: The polling interval and maximum polling duration.
Whether POST /v1/events requires authentication for every request.
correctAnswer: The polling interval and maximum polling duration.
exercises.explanation: The quickstart states the 202 and authentication behavior but explicitly leaves polling bounds undefined.

performanceTask.title: Explain and plan the integration
performanceTask.scenario: A teammate will implement Pulse tomorrow and needs your English mental model and plan.
performanceTask.baselinePrompt: Read the quickstart once, hide it, then explain how the API works and outline implementation without translating it.
performanceTask.performancePrompt: Write 120–180 words in English: explain the request lifecycle and idempotency, distinguish 429 from 503, identify open questions, and give a four-step implementation/test plan.
performanceTask.modelResponse: Pulse accepts an authenticated event and returns 202, so acceptance is not completion. The client generates one idempotency key per logical event, stores it with the event_id and queries status until processed or failed; reusing the key returns the original event. A 429 means rate limiting, while a 503 means temporary unavailability, and the client respects Retry-After when present. The implementation plan has four steps. First, wrap POST and GET while preserving the key-to-event mapping. Second, test duplicate submissions and failed processing. Third, add status polling only after the API owner confirms cadence and timeout, then test both terminal states. Fourth, handle and test 429 and 503 separately, including Retry-After recovery. The quickstart does not define polling bounds, idempotency-key retention or same-key/different-payload behavior, so I would record those as open questions and confirm them before production.
performanceTask.retryPrompt: Rewrite the mental model in your own words and connect every implementation step to a behavior in the docs.
performanceTask.transferPrompt: A new Jobs API returns 202, exposes job status and uses request tokens for deduplication. Produce a fresh mental model and plan that separates acceptance, rate limiting and temporary unavailability.
performanceTask.reviewPrompt: Read an unseen API quickstart once and explain lifecycle, safety mechanism, failure handling and first implementation plan from memory.

artifacts.title: Pulse quickstart
artifacts.content: POST /v1/events requires a bearer token and unique Idempotency-Key. Acceptance returns 202 with event_id; processing is asynchronous and is not complete at acceptance. Poll GET /v1/events/{event_id}. A 429 response includes Retry-After. A 503 indicates temporary unavailability and may also include Retry-After; it is not proof of rate limiting. Reusing a key returns the original event. Polling cadence and timeout, key retention, and same-key/different-payload behavior are not defined and must be confirmed before production.

retry.title: Pulse reliability notes
retry.brief: Repair the weakest part of your mental model with focused evidence.

artifacts.title: Reliability contract
artifacts.content: 202 means accepted, not processed. Store event_id and one key per logical event. Poll until processed or failed. When a 429 response includes Retry-After, wait for that interval and do not create a new key for the same logical event.

artifacts.title: Jobs quickstart
artifacts.content: POST /v2/jobs requires X-Request-Token and returns 202 with job_ref; acceptance is not completion. Query GET /v2/jobs/{job_ref} until complete or failed. Duplicate tokens return the existing job. Rate limiting returns 429 with Retry-After. Temporary unavailability returns 503 and may also include Retry-After; a 503 is not proof that the caller exceeded a rate limit.

artifacts.title: Exports quickstart
artifacts.content: POST /exports accepts a report request and returns 202 with export_id; acceptance is not completion. Supply Client-Request-Id to deduplicate. Poll /exports/{export_id}; download_url appears only at ready. On 429, wait for Retry-After before polling again.

trainingSource.title: Quanta Tasks API
trainingSource.content: POST /tasks requires Authorization and Request-Key. It returns 202 plus task_id; acceptance is not completion. Poll GET /tasks/{task_id} until done or failed. Reusing Request-Key returns the original task. When the service returns 429, wait for Retry-After. The polling interval and maximum polling duration are not defined; confirm both before production.

extractionItems.question: What does 202 mean here?
options: The task completed and the result is ready
The task was accepted for asynchronous processing
The request was rejected until Authorization is added
extractionItems.correctAnswer: The task was accepted for asynchronous processing
extractionItems.feedback: Acceptance and final completion are separate states.

extractionItems.question: What prevents duplicates?
options: Generate a new key for every retry
Poll GET /tasks/{task_id} until the task is done
Reuse Request-Key for the same logical task
extractionItems.correctAnswer: Reuse Request-Key for the same logical task
extractionItems.feedback: The request key identifies one logical operation.

extractionItems.question: How should 429 be handled?
extractionItems.feedback: The server supplies the backoff interval.
